summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with type 1 diabetes and a history of alcohol use, was admitted with malaise, fatigue, and DKA due to insulin noncompliance and recent alcohol use. She presented with profound hyperglycemia, metabolic acidosis, and acute kidney injury from dehydration. She was treated in the ICU with IV fluids and an insulin drip, then transitioned to subcutaneous glargine and lispro. Her electrolytes and renal function normalized, and she had one episode of mild hypoglycemia. Iron studies revealed iron deficiency anemia, and she was started on ferrous sulfate. No infection was found. She was discharged home on day 4 with adjusted insulin, iron supplementation, and instructions to abstain from alcohol and follow up with her primary care provider.
